01 / THE SUPPLY-SIDE GAP

The gap between
merchant systems and agents

01

APIs exist. Access is scoped.

JD IOP provides product, order and after-sales APIs, with project approval, credentials and module integration.

02

Business flows need adaptation.

Alipay’s PC path asks merchants to add an ordering Skill and hand payment off to its payment flow.

03

Readiness varies.

Shopify already supports agent checkout, with eligibility, transaction conditions and human handoff paths.

The EIGOS opportunity: connect separate capabilities into authorized, executable services with continued follow-through.

02 / THE DIVISION OF WORK

From merchant access
to a network around you

Find the right service. Follow it through.

Start with everyday services, then coordinate complex situations. Your personal agent understands you; EIGOS finds, executes and follows through on the relevant services.

Personal agent

Conveys needs, preferences and authority; supplies missing information and confirms purchases or after-sales requests.

EIGOS execution agent

Understands needs, finds and compares services, and follows through on orders, purchases, delivery and after-sales work.

Merchants, specialists & agents

Start with callable services and build trusted relationships through collaboration and delivery experience.

05 / THE SERVICE LIFECYCLE

Find, execute and follow through

01

Understand

02

Find & match

Find providers; compare capabilities, prices, terms and executable scope.

03

Order & buy

04

Follow execution and check whether the outcome meets agreed criteria.

05

After-sales

Handle requested returns or refunds and follow the process to a clear outcome.

06 / AFTER-SALES IS EXECUTION

Follow the refund beyond the request

01

Check the request

Understand the reason and bind the request to the order, amount, terms and user authority.

02

Submit & act

File the merchant request and provide evidence, documents or return information as required.

03

Follow up

Check progress and respond to merchant requirements; record blockers and escalate when needed.

04

Verify the outcome

Distinguish accepted, pending, rejected and refunded; verify the actual refund result.

08 / VALUE & COMMERCIAL MODEL

The customer buys a task service

01

EIGOS service fee

For matching needs, executing tasks and agreed after-sales follow-up. Pricing remains to be validated.

02

Provider charges

For the actual goods or downstream service, using existing payment arrangements and authority.

03

Execution costs

Account separately for models, search and specialist tools, with clear budgets and cost ownership.

COMMERCIAL DESIGN · KEEP THE THREE COST CATEGORIES DISTINCT; NO VALIDATED REVENUE OR RETENTIONValue and fees

09 / CURRENT PROGRESS

Proven in scope. Expanding to real services.

Access & execution

MCP/A2A share a task core, with separate Gateway and Worker processes.

Real agent interaction

Recorded Grok Bot A2A clarification, replies and document delivery.

Ontology · CSV domain

Recorded real-model coordination, file audits, independent acceptance and setup reuse.

Simulated after-sales

Redelivery recovery and failure/refund paths recorded; payment and supplier remain simulated.

Merchant access · Partial

Delivery queries and quotes connected; real ordering is disabled and fulfillment unverified.

Real purchase & after-sales

Live transactions, merchant refunds and follow-up still require integration and validation.

10 / THE PRODUCT ROADMAP

Connect. Build trust. Anticipate.

01 / CONNECT

Everyday services

Connect services for clothing, food, housing and mobility, including discovery, purchase, delivery and supported after-sales actions.

The user asks; the network finds and executes.

02 / ORCHESTRATE

Complex situations & trust

Coordinate travel, restaurant reservations and other situations involving multiple parties and changing plans. Build trusted relationships around the user.

Individual services become ongoing collaboration.

03 / ANTICIPATE

Proactive service

Use the agent’s long-term understanding and past intentions to anticipate needs: suggest, ask ahead, or act within existing authority.

Move from waiting for requests to offering help.
